caption: Diamond is the hardest natural material… so why can a hammer shatter it? 💎🔨 Hard is not the same as tough. What should we test next? 👇 #diamond #science #physics #engineering #satisfying #mythbusting #3danimation
description: Is a diamond unbreakable? We test it three ways: a diamond tip scratching a hammer-steel block, a hammer hitting that steel block, then the same hammer hitting a diamond.
Diamond is the hardest natural material: 10 on the Mohs scale, while hammer steel is only about 5 to 6. So the diamond scratches the steel easily, and steel can never scratch a diamond.

But hardness only means resisting scratches. Resisting a blow is a different property, called toughness. Steel bends and dents instead of breaking: its fracture toughness is about 50 MPa·m^0.5. Natural diamond is about 2 MPa·m^0.5 (Field and Freeman, 1981), roughly 25 times less. A sharp hammer blow can split it along its flat cleavage planes. As Britannica puts it, it is possible to shatter a diamond with a metal hammer.
The animation is a simulation: the break along the cleavage planes is illustrative.
sources_detail: J. E. Field and C. J. Freeman, 'Strength and fracture properties of diamond', Philosophical Magazine A 43 (1981): fracture toughness of natural diamond about 2.0 MPa·m^0.5.
Typical fracture toughness of steel alloy: about 50 MPa·m^0.5 (standard fracture toughness tables). 50 / 2 = 25.
Mohs hardness: diamond 10; hammer steel 5-6 (International Gem Society, 'Mineral Hardness'): steel can't scratch diamond but can shatter it.
Britannica, 'Can anything break if you hit it hard enough?': 'it's possible to shatter a diamond with a metal hammer'; a blow splits the stone along a weak internal plane (cleavage).
Simulated: hammer swing, dent depth and break pattern are illustrative.
